findings.title: The model-identity check passes for any model id against a real llama-server, so a store can be labelled with one model and embedded by another
`index --backfill-code` does quadratic store work; a no-op repeat run still takes 27 s at 2000 files
Code files with non-ASCII names are never indexed, and nothing reports them
`lookup --file` finds nothing when run from a linked git worktree
The spawned llama-server keeps running after the CLI exits, though the README says engram stops it
A repo registered through a symlinked path indexes fine but `lookup --file` finds nothing
A review harvested from a linked worktree is stored twice and its findings stay after the worktree is removed
In a worktree whose branch has drifted, `pack` lists the changed function as Similar code to itself and drops unrelated symbols
An empty `repos.csv` makes a portfolio index or rebuild silently delete every indexed chunk
`index --rebuild` cannot recover a corrupted store
A tracked symlink in a registered repo pulls files from outside the repo into the store and into packs
Credential-shaped strings reach the agent unredacted through `query`, `nudge` and packs
`pack` exclusion calls realpath once per hit per span; a linked worktree doubles it
Repo-scoped `index` and every `pack` enumerate and read the whole portfolio
Ctrl-C during `index --rebuild` leaves `engram.db.rebuild-tmp` behind
An unreadable or non-UTF-8 `repos.csv` gives tracebacks or a misleading not-registered message
A plain `index` or `pack` during a rebuild exits 0 and its writes are thrown away
Two `index` runs on a brand-new store: one crashes with `database is locked`
`query` and `--reembed-code` print a traceback when the endpoint reports another model
`index` downloads a 26 MB grammar bundle; the README says the model download is the only off-machine call
The CHANGELOG has two Added and two Fixed sections under one Unreleased heading and names the wrong grammar-pack version
Every `embed()` call sends an extra ping embedding request first
`harvest` re-reads the registry and resolves every row for every file
Re-harvesting unchanged review files re-embeds everything
A directory with a hand-made `.git` file claims a registered repo's name, and findings harvested there appear in the real repo's packs
Indexed headings reach terminals and agent context with control bytes and instruction text intact
`memory migrate --apply` copies `@path` import text into the `MEMORY.md` that it wires `CLAUDE.md` to import
A relative `repos.csv` row makes every repository take that row's name
Hostile on-disk state gives tracebacks, the lock file follows symlinks, and one bad review file drops a whole harvest batch
The endpoint check and the HTTP client disagree on the host, and non-HTTP schemes pass
The store file costs about 4.3 MB per (repo, corpus) pair, however few chunks it holds

triage.implementation: held as source evidence; execute only through the Gems port

decisions.note: Accept option 1: use the served model listing; retain per-call validation.
Accept option 1: add the corpus/path index without rebuilding vectors.
Accept option 1: NUL-delimited Git paths; retain unmerged-stage deduplication.
Accept option 1: map worktree-relative file paths to the registered checkout; document indexed line positions.
Accept option 1: document intentional detached reuse; no automatic shutdown or watchdog.
Accept option 1 with legacy-memory slug preservation and safe re-indexing of alias code/prose.
Accept canonical identity for future harvests; remove only proven identical legacy aliases and retain differing history.
Accept name/kind identity across distinct checkouts with a reported conservative fallback for ambiguous files.
Accept option 1: refuse an empty registry before pruning or rebuild replacement. The report title overstates loss: findings survive.
Accept explicit discard recovery only, with a retained database backup; default remains loss-averse.
Accept option 1 across enumerators and direct pack inputs; explicit diff input remains permitted.
Accept output redaction and private creation modes, extended to full PEM blocks and quoted credential assignments. Raw existing stores remain.
Accept option 1: canonicalize each distinct path once.
Accept option 1 before code and prose enumeration; retain scope-safe pruning.
Accept finally cleanup under the acquired lock; do not touch another writer's temp.
Accept registry validation with path-specific diagnostics and per-file harvest failures.
Choose option 2: hold the lock through writes. A fail-fast precheck alone has a race.
Accept atomic schema/vector initialization or clean busy refusal; retain a two-process regression.
Accept with model-identity work as mocked error-path coverage; no promotion to live-server verification.
Accept option 1: document model and per-version grammar downloads.
Accept option 2: merge unreleased categories and correct the pin; do not invent a release/tag.
Defer probe caching. Identity correctness comes first; revisit only after model/restart tests and a current workload measurement.
Accept one validated registry snapshot per harvest, shared with the registry fix.
Defer unchanged-harvest caching. First measure whether the actual caller resubmits unchanged files; parser-version invalidation would add state.
Accept option 1: require membership in Git's own worktree list.
Accept control filtering and data framing. This does not guarantee prompt-injection prevention.
Accept conservative migration validation; the downstream import effect remains unverified.
Accept absolute-row validation in the registry reader.
Split by boundary: lock/rebuild issues to 00023; diff physical lines to 00022; parser/config errors to 00025. Narrow transcript claim: ordinary invalid JSON already continues per record.
Accept syntax hardening from a mocked probe. Allow HTTP and HTTPS loopback, reject userinfo/unknown schemes, and validate redirects too.
Accept documentation; retain current vector partitions. Reconsider layout only with disk pressure and measured search/rebuild tradeoffs.
